answers: Never, associated types are always better
When one type should implement the trait several times
writing.exampleCaption: One implementation per type, so the output never has to be annotated.
writing.explanation: A generic parameter lets a type implement a trait many times; an associated type lets it implement it once with a chosen output. Iterator uses Item this way, which is why you write Iterator<Item = u32> rather than passing the element type at every call site.
writing.feedback: From<T> is generic precisely because a type converts from many others.
writing.question: When should you prefer a generic parameter instead?
writing.rule: Associated type: one impl per type. Generic parameter: many impls per type.
writing.success: Callers use the trait without naming the output type.
writing.summary: An associated type fixes one output type per implementation.
